analysis: What changed since the 4 AM brief: three pre-open prints landed. P&G beat revenue ($23.28B vs $22.80B) and maintained full-year guidance while flagging a bigger $1.4B commodity-cost headwind, and the stock is +2% premarket — a genuine non-AI positive. Blackstone is the opposite side of the risk-off tape: exits dried up (net realizations -34%, M&A down 41% sequentially) but $63B+ inflows took AUM to $1.37T. Honeywell raised its full-year outlook on 7% organic growth — an industrial beat being judged on results, in contrast to the AI complex being judged on spend. That contrast is the signal in this brief: P&G and Honeywell show the market still rewards beats with guidance outside the capex debate, while META's decline deepened (-2.44% per Finnhub as of 07:53 ET) and TSLA/NVDA/semis stayed weak. Futures, the 10Y (~5.085%), and oil are roughly unchanged from the 4 AM read, so the premarket narrative is intact, not worsening. Noise to discount: the NYT Iran-strike-plans item (secondhand, unconfirmed) and the Honeywell read itself is single-sourced to an earnings aggregator — the company release or call confirmation is the real confirmation. USAC remains quiet with the Nov 3 earnings and Nov 6 payout on deck.

LRCX (7) bearish: modest beat insufficient for valuation. Agrees with the futures tape, adds no new facts. HN search returned no fresh threads on these names.

headlines.headline: Q3: revenue $28.05B flat YoY, adjusted EPS $0.48 beat ~$0.44; operating income -56% to $718M as opex rose 39% on AI/robotics; auto revenue -3% to $20.56B; free cash flow swung to +$1.53B vs an expected ~$4.5B burn. Management cut 2026 capex to ~$20B (from $25B+) and pushed external Optimus deliveries to around end-2027. Shares down ~5.3% premarket.
headlines.why_it_matters: The beat came from spending less, not selling more; the capex cut reads as the AI/robotics ramp slipping, which is the bearish signal the stock is pricing.

headlines.headline: Q3: revenue $64.6B (+26% YoY) beat ~$63.3B est; EPS $3.83 beat ~$3.57 but carried a $9.89B one-time legal charge (Aug 2026 settlement with 52 state AGs over teen mental health; ex-charge EPS $7.40). Q4 revenue guided $73-76B vs ~$73.6B consensus; 2026 capex narrowed to $135-145B; board approved a non-voting Class C share structure via conditional one-for-one stock dividend. Q3 capex was $34.9B and free cash flow turned negative at -$2.12B. Premarket decline deepened to -2.44% ($680.48 as of 07:53 ET per Finnhub).
headlines.why_it_matters: Revenue beat plus solid guide is a tailwind, but funding the AI build with new equity while FCF goes negative keeps the debate on financing, not growth — the after-hours pop is fully faded.

headlines.headline: FRESH since 4 AM brief — fiscal Q1 (Sep quarter): net sales $23.28B (+4% YoY, beat ~$22.80B est), organic sales +4%, core EPS $2.00 (+1%); volumes +2.4% on beauty/self-care demand. Raised the fiscal-year commodity-cost headwind to ~$1.4B (from $1B) — higher fuel, raw material and transport costs, with US retail diesel at a record $6/gal in September — but maintained FY organic sales, EPS growth and cash-return guidance; updated net sales guidance for the Thorne acquisition. Shares +2% premarket.
headlines.why_it_matters: Revenue beat plus maintained guidance outweighs the bigger cost guide for staples; the $1.4B cost raise is a clean read on tariff/fuel inflation pressure into Q4.

headlines.headline: FRESH since 4 AM brief — Q3: distributable earnings $1.32/share (-13%); net realizations -34% to ~$332M as choppy markets and a 41% sequential drop in global M&A activity slowed exits; cushioned by $63B+ of net inflows pushing AUM to $1.37T and fee-related earnings +6%. Private-credit BCRED redemption requests remained elevated but management says fundamentals are healthy.
headlines.why_it_matters: Exits are the weak link in a risk-off tape, but record inflows shift the focus to fee durability — the alt-manager story is now about fundraising, not harvesting.
